body: Rocket: Robot on Wheels is Sucker Punch Productions' Nintendo 64 platformer about a maintenance robot rescuing a theme park from sabotage. Rocket searches for stolen tickets and tokens while pursuing Jojo, a raccoon who has taken the park's walrus mascot. The themed areas contain rides, vehicles and objects that can be manipulated to solve problems. Rather than rely only on jumping between platforms, the player has to consider how things move and interact, giving a playful mechanical purpose to the robot's work inside the park.

Physics gives movable objects behaviour that needs to be understood before a puzzle can be solved reliably. Mass, friction and inertia make the result depend on how something is handled as well as where it is placed. Each area supplies a vehicle and a collection of tasks, with tickets opening further worlds and tokens purchasing abilities. A ride or machine can become another route to a reward. The player learns the park by using its attractions and discovering what a familiar object can do in a different arrangement.

The studio developed a prototype before securing Nintendo development hardware and spent much of the project looking for a publisher. Ubisoft eventually released the finished game in 1999. Julian Soule composed its music. The amusement-park setting helps explain the mixture of physical experiments, vehicles and platforming routes: each area can introduce another contraption without leaving the same larger place. Rocket's role as a maintenance machine makes manipulating those systems feel like part of the character's work, with recovering the park providing a reason to keep experimenting.
